q-24659.name: Question 1
q-24659.worked_solution:
The roots of $g(z)$ are the solutions to the equation $g(z)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{z}^{3}+5{z}^{2}-z-5}{{z}^{3}+6{z}^{2}+5z}=0.
$$

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(z) & =\frac{{z}^{3}+5{z}^{2}-z-5}{{z}^{3}+6{z}^{2}+5z} \\  & =\frac{{z}^{2}(z+5)-(z+5)}{z({z}^{2}+6z+5)} \\  & =\frac{({z}^{2}-1)(z+5)}{z(z+1)(z+5)} \\  & =\frac{(z+1)(z-1)(z+5)}{z(z+1)(z+5)} \\  & =\frac{(z-1)\cancel{(z+1)(z+5)}}{z\cancel{(z+1)(z+5)}} &  \\  & =\frac{z-1}{z}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}z-1=0\,⟹\,z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $g(z)=0$ is $z=1.$

q-24659.html:
Question 1
?

Find the roots of g(z)=z3+5z2−z−5z3+6z2+5z.

a
z=−5,1
b
z=−2,−1
c
z=1
d
z=−2
e
z=−5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The roots of g(z) are the solutions to the equation g(z)=0. In our case, we have

z3+5z2−z−5z3+6z2+5z=0.

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

g(z)=z3+5z2−z−5z3+6z2+5z=z2(z+5)−(z+5)z(z2+6z+5)=(z2−1)(z+5)z(z+1)(z+5)=(z+1)(z−1)(z+5)z(z+1)(z+5)=(z−1)(z+1)(z+5)z(z+1)(z+5)=z−1z

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for z:

z−1=0⟹z=1

Therefore, the solution to g(z)=0 is z=1.

q-24751.name: Question 2
q-24751.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =\frac{6{u}^{2}+6u-36}{3{u}^{2}+9u} \\  & =\frac{6({u}^{2}+u-6)}{3u(u+3)} \\  & =\frac{6(u+3)(u-2)}{3u(u+3)} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot \cancel{3(u+3)}(u-2)}{u\cdot \cancel{3(u+3)}} \\  & =\frac{2(u-2)}{u}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(u-2) & =0\,⟹\,u=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to $f(u)=0$ is $u=2.$

q-24751.html:
Question 2
?

Solve f(u)=0 where f(u)=6u2+6u−363u2+9u.

a
u=−3,2
b
u=2
c
u=−3
d
u=−3,−12
e
u=−12
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors, as follows:

f(u)=6u2+6u−363u2+9u=6(u2+u−6)3u(u+3)=6(u+3)(u−2)3u(u+3)=2⋅3(u+3)(u−2)u⋅3(u+3)=2(u−2)u

Now, we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for u: 2(u−2)=0⟹u=2

Therefore, the solution to f(u)=0 is u=2.

q-25305.name: Question 3
q-25305.worked_solution:
The roots of $f(h)$ are the solutions to the equation $f(h)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{3{h}^{2}+18}{{h}^{2}+10h+25}=0.
$$

First, we factor $f(h),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(h) & =\frac{3{h}^{2}+18}{{h}^{2}+10h+25} \\  & =\frac{3({h}^{2}+6)}{(h+5)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $h:$

$$
3({h}^{2}+6)=0
$$

Since ${h}^{2}+6>0$ for all $h,$ there is no real solution to $f(h)=0.$ Therefore, $f(h)$ has no real roots.

Question 3
?

Find the roots of f(h)=3h2+18h2+10h+25.

a
h=−5
b
h=−6
c
h=1,2
d
No real roots
e
h=−3,0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The roots of f(h) are the solutions to the equation f(h)=0. In our case, we have

3h2+18h2+10h+25=0.

First, we factor f(h), as follows: f(h)=3h2+18h2+10h+25=3(h2+6)(h+5)2

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for h:

3(h2+6)=0

Since h2+6>0 for all h, there is no real solution to f(h)=0. Therefore, f(h) has no real roots.
